# lean-pkg search

prior-art search over claims, the index and public sources.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg search [--package PACKAGE] [--offline] [--loogle] [--loogle-query PATTERN]
                [--require-complete] [--cache-dir DIR] [--sources a,b,c] [--index INDEX]
                [--record] [--repo DIR] [--agent AGENT] [common flags] TERM
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

Prior-art search. Packages without synced claims are searched by declaration (fully qualified names; accents folded). A source that skipped, failed in part, listed fewer matches than it found or could not read everything makes the search incomplete (complete: false): a zero there is not an absence.

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `TERM` | what to look for (quote a phrase) |
| `--package PACKAGE` | the registered package this search is for (it labels the output; every package's claims are still searched) |
| `--offline` | skip every network source |
| `--loogle` | send the term to Loogle even when it reads as natural language (by default only declaration/type patterns go to Loogle) |
| `--loogle-query PATTERN` | send PATTERN to Loogle instead of the term (a Lean name, term or pattern such as 'Real.exp' or '?a \* ?b = ?b \* ?a'); the other sources still get the term |
| `--require-complete` | exit 1 when the search is incomplete (a source skipped, failed in part, capped, or read only part of what it should); the output is printed in full first |
| `--cache-dir DIR` | use DIR as the lean-pkg cache for this search (Palomar snapshots, Reservoir index) instead of $XDG_CACHE_HOME/lean-pkg or ~/.cache/lean-pkg |
| `--sources a,b,c` | subset of: registry,index,loogle,leansearch,reservoir,palomar,github (order is fixed) |
| `--index INDEX` | index root (default: $LEAN_PKG_INDEX, else ./index) |
| `--record` | write docs/prior-art/&lt;date&gt;-&lt;slug&gt;.md in the package checkout (or --repo) and a prior-art-searched event |
| `--repo DIR` | research repository for --record (old spelling --repo-dir, kept working) |
| `--agent AGENT` | with --record: the agent acting (recorded as the event's actor); another agent's live lease on --package then refuses |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `search TERM` | prior-art search in the fixed order registry, index, loogle, leansearch, reservoir, palomar, github; each source `ok` or `skipped: <reason>`; the registry source scores each package's name (exact name 3), notes, owner_project and repo as well as its cached claims, and every local hit carries `hit_kind` (`package` or `claim`) and `repo`; a conditional claim (one that lists `hypotheses`, or an index claim whose derived `status` is `conditional`) reads `(<kind>, <status> (conditional), trust ...)` and its `--json` hit gains `conditional: true`, as `claims list` marks it ([conditional claims](../prior-art.md#conditional-claims)); a package without synced claims (no cached claim: `claims` coverage `empty`, `unsynced` or `none`) is searched by declaration instead: `git grep` over the tracked `*.lean` files of its checkout at HEAD, every query word (case- and accent-insensitive on both sides: `ito` finds `Itô`; file names with non-ASCII characters are searched) in a `theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|abbrev|inductive|axiom|opaque|irreducible_def` name or its `/-- -/` docstring (a scanner that skips block comments, line comments and strings and reads attributes, modifiers, `instance (priority := n)`, `class inductive`, `class abbrev` and «» names, and skips lines inside a syntax quotation), `decl` the fully qualified name (`namespace`/`section`/`end` tracked one name component at a time, as Lean does; a dotted query such as `DemoA.heatFlowMass_le` is matched against it, a plain query against the name as written), at most 10 listed per package (the rest counted as `declaration_hits_omitted`), reading at most 2000 candidate files per package; a package past that file cap, or with candidate files that could not be read, is listed in `coverage.declaration_files_capped[]` {package, candidates, inspected, unreadable}, named on the coverage line, and makes the search incomplete (the registry block's `incomplete` says why, `truncated_sources: ["registry"]`, `complete: false`); an index entry that cannot be read (invalid YAML, not UTF-8) is counted in the index block's `reason` and `incomplete` and makes the search incomplete too (`truncated_sources: ["index"]`); the `--record` page then marks such a source `incomplete:` in its Sources table, never words it `Not found in`, and names it in a `Not fully searched` sentence; `hit_kind: declaration (unclaimed)`, trust `none`, `file` as `PATH:LINE`, `pin` the HEAD commit, ranked after the claim and package hits; a registered package whose checkout lies inside another's is scanned only as itself (the outer package's scan excludes it); a registered package the registry cannot search (no path, no checkout, no git HEAD, a scan error) is not searched and makes the search incomplete: the registry block's `incomplete` counts them by reason (`2 registered package(s) not searched (no checkout: 1, no git HEAD: 1)`, no names), `truncated_sources` gains `registry`, `complete` is false, `--require-complete` exits 1 and the `--record` page names the registry under `Not fully searched`, never `Not found in` (a package searched by declaration only was searched and leaves it complete); when any source was skipped, the line just before `consulted:` reads `incomplete: searched N of M sources; skipped: A, B; a zero here is not a negative result`, and `--json` always carries `complete` (no source skipped or truncated), `searched` and `skipped_sources[]`; a source that answered with a part failed (GitHub's `code` or `repository` search) stays `ok` but lists the part in its block's `partial[]`, is added to `truncated_sources` and makes the search incomplete (`incomplete: github: code search failed; ...`); a part that returned exactly its result limit (GitHub's `--limit 30`, no paging) lists the part in the block's `capped[]` with `cap_limit` (distinct from `partial[]`, which means failed), is added to `truncated_sources` too (`incomplete: github: code search returned its 30-result limit; ...`, `consulted: ... github (capped, 30 hits)`); a source that found more matches than it lists (Palomar and Reservoir list 30, Loogle 20) reports `capped: ["results"]` with `cap_limit` (the number listed) and `total` (the number found) and is truncated the same way (`incomplete: palomar: 50 matches found, first 30 listed`), and the `--record` page marks it `capped: ...` in its Sources table with an `Incomplete: ... more matches may exist than the ones listed.` sentence; the registry coverage line before that names the blind sources (`registry coverage: 26 of 31 packages have no synced claims: 24 searched by declaration only, 2 not searched (no checkout: ...)`), grouped by reason when several apply (`no path: A; no checkout: B; no git HEAD: C; scan error: D`), and `--json` carries `coverage` (`claims`, `declaration_only`, `not_searched[]` (names, as before), `not_searched_reasons[]` {package, code: `no-path`|`no-checkout`|`no-git-head`|`scan-error`, remedy} whose remedy names only read-only commands keyed by the package name, never a host path, `declaration_hits_omitted`; `null` when the registry was skipped); exit 0 even with zero hits; the term is routed by shape: a Lean declaration or type pattern (`signature`) goes to Loogle, natural language (`natural-language`) skips Loogle with the reason `natural-language query; Loogle takes declaration patterns — try e.g. ...` and still runs every other source; `--loogle` forces Loogle; `--json` carries `route` at the top and on every source; after `--record` writes the page in a repository with an `mkdocs.yml` (or `mkdocs.yaml`) it prints `note: <path> is new; a strict MkDocs build needs a nav entry (or a literate-nav glob) for it` and `--json` carries `nav_hint` (`path`, `reason`); without one there is no note, `nav_hint` is `null` and `record.mkdocs` is `false`; `mkdocs.yml` is never edited; `--loogle-query PATTERN` sends PATTERN (a Lean name, term or pattern) to Loogle instead of the term, whatever the route, and every other source still gets the term (`--json` `loogle_query`); a Loogle parse error ("Unknown identifier ...") is skipped with a reason that says to pass the Lean part that way; `--require-complete` exits 1 when `complete` is false, after printing the full output (`--json` `ok: false` and `error`); a `scan-error` entry carries `detail` (`git grep exit 128: <fixed cause>` or `git grep killed by signal N`, never git's stderr), also shown on the coverage line; an online search refreshes the Palomar snapshot and Reservoir index cache under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/lean-pkg` even without `--record` (never the registry): each block's `cache_writes[]`, `--json` `cache` {`root`, `writes[]`} and a `cache: wrote ...` line say so, and `--cache-dir DIR` keeps that search's cache in DIR; see [Prior-art search](../prior-art.md) | `[--package NAME]` `[--offline]` `[--sources a,b,c]` `[--loogle]` `[--loogle-query PATTERN]` `[--require-complete]` `[--cache-dir DIR]` `[--record]` `[--repo DIR]` `[--index PATH]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## Examples

Search for prior art in the registry, the index, Loogle, LeanSearch, Reservoir, Palomar and GitHub, in that order (Loogle only for a declaration pattern), with each source marked ok or skipped; exit 0 even with zero hits.

```bash
lean-pkg search "heat mass" --package my-proof
```

Skip every network source; as always, packages without synced claims are searched by declaration, and the incomplete line says a zero is not a negative result (add --require-complete to exit 1 then).

```bash
lean-pkg search "heat mass" --offline
```

Sample output:

```text
lean-pkg search "heat mass" on 2026-10-25
registry: ok at sha256:fff31473c971, 1 hit
  [1 name] my-proof: heat_mass_le  (theorem, declaration (unclaimed), trust none, MyProof/Basic.lean:1)
      theorem heat_mass_le : True := trivial
index: skipped: no index directory
loogle: skipped: offline
leansearch: skipped: offline
reservoir: skipped: offline
palomar: skipped: offline
github: skipped: offline
registry coverage: 1 of 1 packages have no synced claims: 1 searched by declaration only, 0 not searched (no checkout)
incomplete: searched 1 of 7 sources; skipped: index, loogle, leansearch, reservoir, palomar, github; a zero here is not a negative result
consulted: registry (ok, 1 hit), index (skipped: no index directory), loogle (skipped: offline), leansearch (skipped: offline), reservoir (skipped: offline), palomar (skipped: offline), github (skipped: offline)
```

Also write docs/prior-art/&lt;date&gt;-&lt;slug&gt;.md (decision pending) in the package's checkout and a prior-art-searched event; edit the page, then commit it in that repository.

```bash
lean-pkg search heat_mass_le --package my-proof --record
```
